subject: surgery
title: Andrology and male infertility: ED, varicocele and azoospermia

steps.tx: **Erectile dysfunction** is most often vasculogenic, and **sildenafil** remains first line treatment when the morning testosterone is normal. Nitrates must never combine with a PDE5 inhibitor because the pair drops blood pressure dangerously. Low morning testosterone needs replacement, while psychogenic disease in young men needs counselling. Vacuum devices, alprostadil injections, and finally a penile prosthesis complete the ladder, and erectile dysfunction also predicts cardiovascular disease.
steps.say: Erectile dysfunction is most often vasculogenic in older men. Sildenafil remains first line treatment when testosterone is normal. Nitrates must never combine with this treatment class dangerously. Low morning testosterone needs replacement after confirmation testing. Psychogenic disease in young men needs counselling first. Devices, injections, and a prosthesis form the final rungs of treatment.

steps.tx: A **varicocele** feels like a bag of worms on standing, occurs mainly on the **left side**, and is graded by Valsalva examination and visibility. Ligation or coil embolisation improves semen quality, and adolescent testicular hypotrophy supports operation. The same scrotal examination separates epididymitis, mumps orchitis, and a transilluminating **hydrocele**. **Testicular torsion** with a bell clapper deformity remains a surgical emergency needing immediate detorsion.
steps.say: A varicocele feels like a bag of worms on standing. The lesion occurs mainly on the left side clinically. Grading uses Valsalva examination and visibility together. Ligation or embolisation improves semen quality afterward. Torsion remains an emergency needing immediate detorsion surgery. Hydrocele transilluminates brightly during scrotal examination today.

steps.tx: **Azoospermia** means no sperm appear even after centrifugation of **two semen samples**, and follicle stimulating hormone separates the two main causes. Obstructive disease shows normal hormone levels, normal testes, and a palpable vas deferens. Non obstructive disease shows high hormone levels with small testes, and genetics includes Klinefelter syndrome, Y microdeletions, and CFTR testing. Retrieval by PESA, TESA, or micro TESE feeds directly into **ICSI** treatment.
steps.say: Azoospermia means no sperm appear after centrifugation twice. Two semen samples confirm the finding before further testing. Hormone levels separate obstructive from non obstructive causes clearly. Obstructive disease keeps normal testes and palpable vas deferens. Non obstructive disease presents with small testes and high hormone levels. Retrieval techniques provide sperm directly for ICSI treatment.

steps.tx: The left panel shows **obstructive azoospermia** with a normal sized testis, a dilated epididymis, and a palpable vas despite a focal duct block. The right panel shows **non obstructive azoospermia** with a small atrophic testis and hyalinised seminiferous tubules. **FSH** is normal on the left and elevated on the right. Two empty semen samples below confirm azoospermia before either pathway begins.
steps.say: The left panel shows obstruction with a normal sized testis. A dilated epididymis and palpable vas accompany the blockage. The right panel presents a small atrophic testis instead. Hyalinised tubules explain failure of sperm production there. Hormone levels separate the two pathways before retrieval planning.

steps.tx: Premature ejaculation responds to behavioural squeeze methods and **SSRIs**, while **delayed ejaculation** needs review of causative drugs first. Retrograde ejaculation in diabetes may respond to sympathomimetic drugs, and anejaculation after spinal injury may need vibratory stimulation. **Vasectomy** needs semen clearance before reliance, and reversal success falls as years pass. Morning testosterone assessment completes hypogonadism evaluation when fertility plans allow replacement.
steps.say: Premature ejaculation improves with squeeze methods and drug treatment. Delayed ejaculation needs careful review of causative drugs first. Retrograde ejaculation in diabetes may respond to sympathomimetic treatment. Spinal anejaculation may need vibratory stimulation afterward. Vasectomy needs semen clearance before contraceptive reliance begins. Morning testosterone assessment completes hypogonadism evaluation carefully.
